title: legal redlines scratchpad - isabella
content:
Personal scratchpad for contract redlines / negotiation points — working notes (informal).

Quick context:
- Customer: enterprise fintech prospect (on-prem eval + hosted API trial).
- Commercial ask: standard enterprise T&Cs + data isolation guarantees, audit rights, 99.9% uptime SLA, breach notification windows, and restrictions on downstream model training/use of customer prompts and outputs.
- Goal: protect Redwood IP and runtime optimizations while minimizing obligation to customers around data deletion/retention and model training.

Top clauses to watch (priority order):
1) Data usage / model training clause
   - Customer asks: "We require that you will not use our prompts/data to further train or improve models."
   - Our preferred language: we do not use customer-provided prompts or customer content to train our public models. For hosted offerings, propose explicit opt-in for any training, or clarify that telemetry/aggregated metrics are used only for service reliability and debugging and are pseudonymized.
   - Negotiation points: define "Customer Data" precisely, carve out telemetry/operational logs vs substantive content. Add example list of telemetry we collect (latency, error types, token counts) and confirm no prompting/content is included.

2) Confidentiality (NDA terms embedded)
   - Watch for overly broad definitions (e.g., "all data" without time/retention limits).
   - Push back on perpetual confidentiality for residuals; propose standard residuals carve-out + limited-term secrecy obligations (3-5 years depending on risk).

3) Liability / Indemnity / IP ownership
   - Liability cap: aim for standard (fees paid in prior 12 months or $1M) but be flexible depending on enterprise negotiation.
   - Indemnity: restrict to third-party IP infringement for customer inputs + misuse by customer; avoid broad indemnities for customer outputs.
   - IP ownership: Redwood retains model weights, runtime code, optimizations; customer owns their data and derived outputs (subject to data-usage clause). For hosted models, include language that model-generated outputs are provided "AS IS" and customer is responsible for compliance of downstream use.

4) Security / breach notification / breach response
   - Minimum: notify within 72 hours for confirmed breaches affecting Customer Data.
   - Customer may request penetration test reports / SSAE/SOC3? We can provide SOC2 Type II report; avoid source code or full infra diagrams.

5) Audit rights / access
   - Customers often want broad audit rights. Propose: limited to SOC2 reports and one remote review per year with scope limited to controls affecting Customer Data; on-site audits are allowed only with advance notice and cost recovery.

6) Data retention & deletion / data portability
   - Clarify logs retention periods (e.g., telemetry 90 days, request logs 30 days unless customer requests retention for debugging). For Dedicated/Private deployments, allow customer-controlled retention settings.
   - Provide simple deletion API and confirm deletion "best effort" for backups with documented retention window.

7) SLA / credits / remedies
   - 99.9% uptime standard for Dedicated; hosted tier has lower SLO. Limit remedies to service credits only. No consequential damages. Define measurement and maintenance windows.

8) Export control / sanctions / compliance
   - Add compliance language: both parties must comply with applicable export controls and sanctions; include right to suspend service for sanctioned entities.

9) Subprocessors / subcontractors
   - For hosted, list cloud providers; for Private deployments, state that subcontractors may be used for support but access is limited and controlled. Provide option for customer to opt-out of certain subprocessors in enterprise negotiations — expect pushback.

10) Termination / transition assistance
   - Termination for convenience: 30 days; termination for cause after cure period (30 days). Transition assistance: limited to 90 days after termination with fees for extended support.

Sample suggested redlines / plain language alternatives to propose during negotiation:
- Data usage: "Provider shall not use, access, or incorporate Customer Data into Provider models or training datasets, except with Customer's prior written consent. Provider may collect aggregated telemetry for service operation and performance improvement, provided such telemetry does not include Customer Data or any Personal Data."
- Liability cap: "Provider's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer to Provider under the Agreement in the 12 months preceding the claim, or one million USD (USD $1,000,000), whichever is greater."
- Indemnity carve-outs: "Provider will indemnify Customer for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement to the extent arising from Provider's services. Customer will indemnify Provider for claims arising from Customer Data or Customer's use of the Service in violation of the Agreement."
- Audit: "Customer's audit rights are limited to reviewing Provider's relevant SOC2 Type II report and one remote compliance review per 12-month period. On-site audits require reasonable notice and are subject to Provider's reasonable security requirements and reimbursement of Provider's reasonable costs."

Negotiation playbook (talking points):
- If they insist on training prohibition, offer: formal statement that we do not train on Customer Data by default + contract covenant + optional paid add-on for customers that want training/finetuning with explicit data handling rules.
- For customer wanting low liability cap: trade for higher annual commit or expanded indemnity from customer side; consider providing an SLA uplift in exchange for higher liability cap.
- For audit requests: offer redacted SOC2/pen test summaries; limit frequency and scope.
- For regulatory customers asking for export-controlled features: route to Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) and engage infra/legal for extra controls.

Open TODOs / Notes to self:
- Confirm default log retention windows with infra (ask infra: request-logs retention, KV cache dumps policy). JIRA INF ticket referenced above.
- Check SOC2 artifacts availability and what we can share publicly.
- Draft allowable subprocessors list (GCP/AWS/Azure) with region specifics.
- Confirm breach notification SLA with SRE on call.
- Create short customer-facing explanation doc for data usage (simple FAQ) that legal + DX can use in negotiations.

Examples of customer asks and quick responses (cheat-sheet):
- Customer: "Will you delete all our prompts immediately on request?" -> Answer: "Yes — we provide a deletion API and process deletion within X days; note backups may persist for Y days; for hosted service we can negotiate stricter retention for enterprise contracts."
- Customer: "Can we get on-site code review?" -> Answer: "We don't provide source code reviews. We can provide SOC2 report, architecture diagrams at a high level, and run a mutually agreed security assessment or red-team for a fee."
- Customer: "Can you train the model on our data?" -> Answer: "We do not train on customer data without explicit written consent and separate commercial terms; we can offer dedicated finetuning engagements with controls."

Quick checklist before sending counterparty redline:
- [ ] Confirm retention & deletion text with infra (exact days)
- [ ] Confirm SOC2 availability and latest date
- [ ] Decide on liability cap floor for this ACV range
- [ ] Draft carve-out language for telemetry vs customer data
- [ ] Prepare fallback language for audit/on-site requests

Slack-style quick notes / fragments (keep informal):
- "Call with Acme legal weds 10am PT — bring liability + training scripts"
- "If they push for perpetual confidentiality -> push back hard; limit to 3-5 years and link to contract value/commits"
- "Consider offering 'data processing addendum' template for EU customers covering GDPR + SCCs"

End of scratchpad.

[This is a working doc; not for distribution outside legal/solutions teams. Keep redlines tight and prioritize product safety + IP.]
